topic: A guest running late in the snow

guest.name: 藤原さん
guest.role: a retired teacher from {名古屋|なごや} on a ski trip, very polite

title_jp: {遅れて|おくれて}{着く|つく}お{客|きゃく}さん
context: Monday 14 December: アルちゃん is on reception at ゲストハウス{風|かぜ} when a guest, {藤原|ふじわら}さん, messages the guesthouse LINE: his train is stuck in the snow and he'll arrive after 9 p.m. He politely asks about the bath and a place to eat.
scene: Monday afternoon at reception. A guest messages the guesthouse LINE: his train is stuck in the snow and he has a few requests.

phrases.jp: {恐れ入りますが|おそれいりますが|I'm sorry to trouble you, but|2}、もう{一度|いちど}お{願い|ねがい}できますか。
phrases.en: I'm sorry to trouble you, but could you say that once more?
phrases.note: {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが softens any request at work: a 'cushion word'.

phrases.jp: あと、{一つ|ひとつ}{伺っても|うかがっても|to ask (humble)|3}よろしいですか。
phrases.en: Also, may I ask one more thing?
phrases.note: {伺|うかが}う = humble {聞|き}く. For customers, bosses, teachers.

phrases.jp: {早ければ|はやければ}{早い|はやい}ほどいいです。
phrases.note: A set phrase. Casual: {早|はや}ければ{早|はや}いほどいいよ.

phrases.jp: {到着|とうちゃく|arrival|3}が{遅れそう|おくれそう}です。
phrases.en: It looks like I'll arrive late.
phrases.note: Send this before the time, not after.

phrases.jp: お{待ち|まち}しております。
phrases.en: We look forward to seeing you.
phrases.note: Humble keigo staff use for guests on their way.

dialogue_setting: The guesthouse's LINE account on the reception tablet, late afternoon. Snow outside the window.

dialogue.speaker: 藤原さん
dialogue.jp: ゲストハウス{風|かぜ}さま。{本日|ほんじつ|today (formal)|3}{予約|よやく}している{藤原|ふじわら}です。
dialogue.en: To Guesthouse {風|かぜ}. This is {藤原|ふじわら}, booked for today.

dialogue.speaker: 藤原さん
dialogue.jp: {雪|ゆき}で{電車|でんしゃ}が{止まって|とまって}しまい、{到着|とうちゃく|arrival|3}が9{時|じ}{過ぎ|すぎ|past, after|3}になりそうです。
dialogue.en: The train has stopped because of the snow, so I'll probably arrive after 9.

dialogue.speaker: 藤原さん
dialogue.jp: {恐れ入りますが|おそれいりますが|I'm sorry to trouble you, but|2}、お{風呂|ふろ}は{何時|なんじ}まで{使えますか|つかえますか}。
dialogue.en: Sorry to trouble you, but until what time can I use the bath?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: ご{連絡|れんらく}ありがとうございます。お{風呂|ふろ}のご{利用|りよう|use|3}は10{時|じ}までです。
dialogue.en: Thank you for letting us know. The bath can be used until 10.

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {夜|よる}は{遅く|おそく}なればなるほど{冷えます|ひえます}ので、{暖かく|あたたかく|warm|4}してお{越し|こし}ください。
dialogue.en: The later it gets, the colder it is, so please dress warmly on your way.
dialogue.note: お{越|こ}しください = honorific 'please come'.

dialogue.speaker: 藤原さん
dialogue.jp: {助かります|たすかります}。あと、{一つ|ひとつ}{伺っても|うかがっても|to ask (humble)|3}よろしいですか。
dialogue.en: That's a great help. May I ask one more thing?

dialogue.speaker: 藤原さん
dialogue.jp: {夕食|ゆうしょく|dinner|3}がまだなんです。{遅く|おそく}まで{開いて|あいて}いるお{店|みせ}はありますか。
dialogue.en: I haven't had dinner yet. Is there anywhere open late?

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: {商店街|しょうてんがい}の{とり吉|とりきち}が、11{時|じ}まで{営業|えいぎょう|being open (for business)|3}しています。
dialogue.en: {とり吉|とりきち} on the shopping street is open until 11.

dialogue.speaker: 藤原さん
dialogue.jp: ありがとうございます

dialogue.speaker: アルちゃん
dialogue.jp: お{待ち|まち}しております。お{気をつけて|きをつけて}！
dialogue.en: We look forward to seeing you. Travel safely!

listening.intro: {健太|けんた} phones to check on the late guest and gives you a reception rule.

lines.jp: {連絡|れんらく}は{早ければ|はやければ}{早い|はやい}ほど{ええねん|ええねん|(Kansai) = いいんだ|2}。
lines.en: When it comes to getting in touch, the sooner the better.

grammar.form: verb: ば-form + dictionary form + ほど ({遅|おそ}くなればなるほど, すればするほど) · い-adj: -ければ + -い + ほど ({早|はや}ければ{早|はや}いほど) · な-adj: なら + な + ほど ({静|しず}かなら{静|しず}かなほど)
grammar.explanation: Say the same word twice: the more one thing happens, the more something else follows. First in ば-form, then plain form + ほど. The two must be the same word. You can also drop the ば part: {遅|おそ}くなるほど{冷|ひ}える.

examples.jp: {練習|れんしゅう}すればするほど、{上手|じょうず}になるよ。
examples.en: The more you practise, the better you get.

examples.jp: {考えれば|かんがえれば}{考える|かんがえる}ほど、{分からなく|わからなく}なる。
examples.en: The more I think about it, the less I understand.

quiz.question: {雪|ゆき}が{降れば|ふれば}＿＿ほど、{道|みち}が{混む|こむ}。
quiz.en: The more it snows, the more crowded the roads get.
quiz.explain: After the ば-form, repeat the dictionary form: {降|ふ}れば{降|ふ}るほど.

quiz_more.question: この{温泉|おんせん}は、{入れば|はいれば}{入る|はいる}＿＿{体|からだ}が{温まる|あたたまる|to warm up|3}。
quiz_more.en: The longer you stay in this onsen, the warmer you get.
quiz_more.explain: ば + dictionary form + ほど: 'the more…, the more…'.

quiz_more.question: {部屋|へや}は{広ければ|ひろければ}＿＿ほどいい。
quiz_more.en: The bigger the room, the better.
quiz_more.explain: い-adjectives: -ければ, then the plain -い form + ほど.

kanji.where: On the card by the guesthouse door: {門限|もんげん} 23:00.
kanji.breakdown: 門 gate + 限 limit → the time limit for the gate: curfew.
kanji.related: Students and dorms have one too: {門限|もんげん}は10{時|じ}.

tip.title: Cushion words
tip.body: Japanese wraps a request in a 'cushion word' (クッション{言葉|ことば}) first: {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが, お{手数|てすう}ですが, {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありませんが. Without one, even a perfect keigo request can sound blunt. Guesthouses, {旅館|りょかん} and {民宿|みんしゅく} hear them all day.

challenge.prompt: At 21:20 {藤原|ふじわら}さん arrives safely. {健太|けんた} on LINE: 「お{疲れ|つかれ}！{明日|あした}の{朝食|ちょうしょく}は{俺|おれ}がやるから、アルちゃんはゆっくり{寝て|ねて}な」 Send a sticker to thank him.
challenge.explanation: {健太|けんた} is doing you a favour, so the right feeling is thanks: ありがとう〜. ごめん would mean you did something wrong, and ガーン or {怖|こわ}い don't fit good news.

vocab.note: Formal {今日|きょう}. On shop signs: {本日休業|ほんじつきゅうぎょう} = closed today.
{到着|とうちゃく}する = to arrive. Opposite: {出発|しゅっぱつ}.
9{時|じ}{過|す}ぎ = just after 9. Also {食|た}べ{過|す}ぎ = overeating.

vocab.en: to be sorry to trouble; to be grateful
vocab.note: Almost always {恐|おそ}れ{入|い}りますが, before a request.
{利用|りよう}する = to use (a service). On signs: ご{利用|りよう}ください.
{暖|あたた}かくして = wrap up warm. Warm drinks: {温|あたた}かい.
Humble form of {聞|き}く and {訪|たず}ねる.
Polite {晩|ばん}ご{飯|はん}. Hotels: {夕食付|ゆうしょくつ}き = dinner included.
{営業中|えいぎょうちゅう} = Open on shop doors. {営業時間|えいぎょうじかん} = opening hours.

kanji_study.parts: 禾 grain + 刂 knife → cutting the ripe grain at harvest: what you gain, something useful.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 和 (peace, Japanese): 和 has 口 a mouth on the right, 利 has 刂 a knife.

kanji_study.parts: An old drawing of an eye pierced by a needle, a mark once put on servants → the common people.
kanji_study.lookalike: Not 氏 (family name, Mr): 民 has an extra box at the top left.

extras.title: Cushion words
extras.title_jp: クッション{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: Say one before any request at work.

items.jp: お{手数|てすう|trouble, bother|2}ですが、こちらにお{名前|なまえ}をお{願い|ねがい}します。
items.en: Sorry for the trouble, but your name here, please.
items.note: For asking someone to do a task.

items.jp: {申し訳|もうしわけ|excuse, apology|3}ありませんが、{満室|まんしつ|fully booked|2}です。
items.en: I'm very sorry, but we're fully booked.

items.jp: よろしければ、お{茶|ちゃ}をどうぞ。
items.en: If you'd like, please have some tea.

extras.title: Places to stay
extras.intro: What you'll see on booking sites.

items.note: Tatami rooms, dinner and breakfast often included.
Cheaper, homely, often in the countryside.

items.jp: {素泊まり|すどまり|room only (no meals)|2}
